title: What Your Credit Card Does at Midnight
description:
ZERO pays the minimum on his first credit card bill at 11:58 PM. At midnight, his balance goes up. So time stops, and he follows the number he still owes into the machine that adds to it every night: the grace period, the yearly rate, the divide-by-365 and interest on interest. Then he zooms out to see who pays for the rewards, and what paying a little more changes.

Zero doesn't know how the world works. Yet.

Chapters
0:00 11:58 PM: the minimum payment
0:11 At midnight, his balance went up
0:27 Inside the machine: the calendar
0:36 The grace period
0:55 Interest on what he still owes
1:04 22.36% a year, divided by 365
1:28 Sixty cents a night
1:47 Thirty nights later
2:10 Only a third of the payment reaches the debt
2:18 The coffee and its cash back
3:06 Who pays, who gets the rewards
3:46 Late fees and persistent debt
4:00 The box on every statement
4:09 Paying $100 a month instead
4:27 Next month, 11:58 PM
4:43 Was this you?

Every number in this video has a source. FACT = stated by the source; ESTIMATE = our calculation or a model, rounded; ILLUSTRATION = how it can look, not a real bank's rules.
- 22.36% average rate on accounts charged interest, Aug 2026 (FACT): Federal Reserve G.19, Oct 7 2026 https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/g19/current/g19.pdf
- Interest is calculated daily: yearly rate / 365 = 0.0613% a day; about 60 cents a night on $975 and about $18.08 in 30 nights (ESTIMATE, our calculation, interest on interest included).
- Minimum payment of 1% of the balance plus the month's interest = about $27.83 (ILLUSTRATION: each issuer sets its own formula); about a third of it reduces the debt (ESTIMATE).
- Paying only the minimum: about 69 months and about $735 in interest; paying $100 a month: about 11 months and about $94 (ESTIMATE, our own model on $1,000 at 22.36% with no new purchases).
- Pay the full statement by the due date and there is generally no interest; the statement arrives at least 21 days before the due date (FACT): CFPB, "What is a grace period?" https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-grace-period-en-47/
- $105 billion in interest and $14.5 billion in late fees in 2022; 94% of interest and fees paid by people who carry a balance, who earn 27% of rewards, versus 73% for people who pay in full (FACT): CFPB, "The Consumer Credit Card Market", 2023 https://www.consumerfinance.gov/data-research/research-reports/the-consumer-credit-card-market-2023/
- About 1 in 10 cardholders is in persistent debt (FACT, CFPB report above).
- Every statement shows a minimum-payment warning box with the months and total cost of paying only the minimum (FACT): Credit CARD Act of 2009.
- ZERO's 5-cent cash back is about 17 days of his own interest (ESTIMATE).
The $1,000 bill, the $25 payment, the 60-cent coin, the café and the $479.99 charge are part of the story, not claims.
